div.div: شُكْرَةٌ (assumed tropical:) [Fulness of the udder of a camel; and so ↓ شَكَرِيَّةٌ is expl. in the TK;] a subst. from أَشْكَرَ القَوْمُ [q. v.]. (K.) One says, هٰذَا زَمَنُ الشُّكْرَةِ, so in the L and other lexicons, (TA,) or ↓ الشَّكَرَةِ , (so in my copies of the S,) or ↓ الشَّكَرِيَّةِ , (so in the O and K,) (assumed tropical:) [This is the time of the fulness of the udder,] when the camels abound with milk, or have their udders full, (إِذَا حَفَلَتْ, q. v.,) from the [herbage called] رَبِيع. (S, O, L, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
